content: Common mistake when retrofitting OAuth onto a system built around one static shared secret: swapping the shared token for a single long-lived JWT/service credential reproduces the exact same problem (non-revocable, no per-identity scoping) with a false sense of having 'added security'. Correct pattern decouples a long-lived credential (client secret) from short-lived, revocable, audience-bound access tokens, and migrations fail operationally when redirect-URI/config changes aren't coordinated across all consumers before cutover.
